transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
Well… since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. I’m up and moving all day, going from one little job to the next, like there’s still a crew waiting on me or something.
When you’re going from one task to the next like that, do you feel unusually energetic?
I don’t know if I’d call it energetic exactly. I just… I’m up and moving all day, going from one little thing to the next. Feels like I’m still supposed to be keeping busy.
Do unwanted thoughts keep popping into your mind that make you feel like you have to keep doing these little jobs?
Not really… I wouldn’t say it’s unwanted thoughts. It’s more just, I notice something needs doing and I go do it. I don’t know.
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?
I don’t think so. Sleep’s about the same, far as I can tell.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot?
I don’t know… not a lot, I wouldn’t say. I mean, I think about things, sure, but I haven’t really noticed worrying all the time.
Have there been times when you felt unusually happy or high for no clear reason?
No… I don’t think so. I mean, I have decent moods sometimes, but not unusually high or anything like that.
Did this start after you stopped working?
Yeah… I guess it got to be a real problem after I retired from handyman work. That was about a year and a couple months ago.
Does it feel like this mostly started because of retiring?
Yeah… mostly after I retired, I’d say. It was about a year and two months ago, and that’s when it started feeling like more of a real problem.
Does this leave you feeling distressed?

Yeah… it does. I don’t like admitting it, but my wife’s had to start keeping the calendar and checking behind me. And I’ve had to apologize to folks at the community center and the garden group more than once for dropping the ball. It’s embarrassing.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of different things?
I don’t know… not really a lot of different things, no. I get bothered by certain stuff, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all the time.
Do you feel this started because retiring was hard for you to adjust to?
I guess… maybe. It really became a problem after I stopped doing handyman work, about a year and a couple months ago. Before that, I didn’t think much of it.
Have these problems made it hard for you to keep up with your usual responsibilities?

Yeah… some. My wife’s had to take over the calendar and kind of check behind me. And I’ve had to go back and apologize to people at the community center and the garden group when I let things slip. It’s not great.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?
Yeah… a bit. If I’m painting, or trying to plan out a story, and I hear a truck outside or I remember something in the garden, my mind just goes over there. Then I’ve lost where I was.
Do you feel most of this has been about adjusting to retirement?
Maybe partly, yeah. I just know it really started feeling like a problem after I retired from the handyman work… about a year and a couple months ago.
Have these problems lasted more than six months since your retirement?
Yeah. It’s been more than six months. I’d say it started being a real problem after I retired from the handyman work… about a year and two months ago.
If you had not retired, do you think these problems would still be happening?

I think so, yeah. I mean… it’s not brand new. Even when I was a kid, teachers would say I was smart but scattered—losing pencils, blurting things out, needing reminders to finish my work before recess. So… retirement maybe made it more noticeable, but it was there before.
